RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Drawn on the wrong side at Royal Ascot on handicap debut and was a heavily backed winner at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, when making most; he did it in good style and a 9lb rise may not stop him this afternoon; ran well on good to soft last August, unraced on softer.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Made it three wins from his last four starts when returning to winning ways at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last month; had just a nose to spare and is 6lb higher today, but all of his wins have been narrow ones and he keeps defying the handicapper; has run well on good to soft (unraced on softer).

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won handicap debut at Ascot (1m, good) in May and second of 30 in the Britannia at the Royal meeting there (1m, good to firm) in June; he's 5lb higher than last time but is unexposed and could have plenty more to offer; firmly in calculations; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
OwnerName: James Paul Services To Industry Ltd
Spotlight: 2yo Listed winner in France (1m, very soft) and, having been gelded, he was back on song at Ripon (1m, good to firm) last month when first past the post (demoted to third due to interference); slow ground would hold no fears but it was a small field last time and this race is much hotter.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: All seven starts on good/good to firm; won the competitive Silver Bowl at Carlisle (1m) in May before mid-division at Royal Ascot, and he was a close third of 15 at Glorious Goodwood (1m1f) three weeks ago; could again be in the mix.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Three wins from his five starts, awarded the race at Ripon (1m, good to firm) last month due to interference (Command The Stars demoted); however, it was a small field last time and he could be vulnerable now back into a more competitive contest; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won both 2yo starts and he's improved with each of his four handicap runs this term, finishing strongly in first-time cheekpieces (retained) for 1l second of 19 to Exclusive Code at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; respected despite 5lb rise; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Returned to winning ways at Pontefract (1m, good) last month and found a surge of improvement to follow up by 7l against 13 runners at Redcar (1m, good to firm); he's 11lb higher than last time and in a higher grade but it remains to be seen where his limitations now lie; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: 2-2 in France last year (6.5f/1m, soft/very soft); yet to pose a threat in Britain but he kept on from the rear for 4l 11th of 19 behind Exclusive Code at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, which was encouraging, and he could be a serious force on today's slower ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won at Chester (7.5f, good to soft) in June and ran well off this 5lb higher mark when 1l fourth of 11 at Thirsk (1m, good) three weeks ago; further improvement can't be ruled out but it's necessary if he's to return to winning ways in this hotter contest.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Two 2yo wins (including on soft ground) and back on the scoresheet at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last month; another big run when second of 13 at Glorious Goodwood (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago; he's a headstrong sort but that didn't stop him finishing strongly last time and this first crack at 1m is well worth a go; he's one to consider.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: All four starts on good/good to firm; posted her second win on handicap debut at Ayr (1m, good) last month; had just a neck to spare and is 5lb higher up in grade this afternoon, but that form has been franked by the placed horses and he could have more left in the tank.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt in Ripon novice (1m, good) in June, showing improved form and defying trouble in running to win comfortably on his second start since being gelded; his dam was a 1m2f Listed winner (on soft ground) and he has the potential to be better than his opening mark.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Consistent sort who won Dundalk maiden (1m, AW) last month on his seventh start before close third on handicap debut at Galway (8.5f, yielding); he kicked clear turning for home last time and today's slightly shorter trip could be a positive; cheekpieces replace blinkers; each-way possibilities.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Heavy-ground 2yo maiden winner who came from a tough position to win valuable final here (7f, good) last October; hasn't kicked on this season but he returned to his best with close second of six at Newmarket last month (1m, good to firm; ran minus a plate); worth a second look given his course form.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Placed on his first four starts (including on soft) and got going too late in first-time cheekpieces (retained) when sixth of 19 to Exclusive Code on handicap debut at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good to firm); a stronger gallop today would help his cause and he's not discounted.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: It was a small field at Ripon (1m, good to firm) in which he returned to form last time, when battling it out with Command The Stars and Noelan Star, and this is much more competitive; however, his two best RPRs have come at York and he's 4lb lower than when second of 14 here (7f, good) in May; could go well at a big price if conditions suit (unproven on slow ground).

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won two in a row at Chester (6f/7f, soft/good) in June and respectable efforts at Chester (7.5f, good) and Glorious Goodwood (7f, good to firm) since; however, he needs something extra on today's first attempt at 1m if he's to land a competitive handicap such as this.

RaceName: Sky Bet Mile Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Well-beaten favourite on debut at Salisbury (7f, soft) in June but left that behind to win in a first-time tongue-tie (retained since) at Kempton (7f, AW); clear second under a penalty at Thirsk (1m, good) three weeks ago and this 450,000gns half-brother to multiple Group/Grade 1 winner Romantic Warrior could be on a good mark for this first handicap start.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 72,000gns yearling by Make Believe; weak 16-1 shot in a maiden at Glorious Goodwood (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago, but she finished well to snatch third behind the two market leaders; that was a striking debut and she sets a good standard on that form; holds a Group 1 entry in the Fillies' Mile.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Stradivarius filly who struggled at 50-1 in a C&D novice (good to firm) on recent debut; opposable.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 200,000euros yearling; half-sister to to three winners including Pierre Bonnard (1m/1m2f 2yo including Group 1; RPR 119) and Crepe Suzette (Group-placed 9.4f AW; 110); ran green when fifth of seven in a C&D novice three weeks ago but that was behind a smart prospect and she wasn't beaten far; should know more this time and she's a likely improver on her second start.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Katy Jane Reed And Edward J Ware
Spotlight: 120,000euros yearling; second foal; dam 1m winner (RPR 98), half-sister to winners Sea La Rosa (1m6f Group 1) and Deauville Legend (1m4f Group 2), out of German 1m3f Listed winning sister to 1m2f Group 2 winner Hanami; plenty to like on paper and yard is 26% with 2yos this season.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: St Mark's Basilica filly; second foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Beat The Bank (multiple 1m Group 2), Chil Chil (6f Group 3) and Auria (1m Listed), out of useful 6f 2yo winner; interesting newcomer and she needs a close look in market.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 110,000gns yearling; fourth foal; sister to winners Quatre Bras (7f 2yo/10.6f AW; RPR 89) and Casa De Salinas (1m AW 2yo; 73); dam 6f-8.4f winner (including AW/Group 3; 104), half-sister to German 1m2f Group 3 winner Waleria; has good standard to aim at on debut and market should guide.

RaceName: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 110,000gns foal, 70,000gns yearling; second foal; half-sister to Italian 1m1f 2yo winner Drago Blues (including Listed; RPR 90); dam French 7f/US 1m winner (96), half-sister to winners Ouraika (US 6.5f Grade 3 turf), Complication (7f) and Santara (German 7.5f 2yo); another well-bred newcomer and the market should point the way.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Not an instant success for new stable this season but won easily by 4l off much-reduced mark at Carlisle (5.8f, good) ten days ago and is 4lb ahead of the handicapper under 5lb penalty here; commands respect.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Battled well to win from the front over C&D (good) 17 days ago, his second success this season; ought to give another good account but recent 2lb nudge could be enough to leave him vulnerable.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Won 5f maiden maiden last summer but ended his 2yo campaign with a disappointing effort and ran as though something was amiss on last month's reappearance; sports new cheekpieces for first attempt at 6f; needs to get career back on track.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Returned to form with clear win in first-time cheekpieces here (5f, good to soft) in early June but has not quite been at the same level on his three starts since and is not yet proven over 6f; goes without headgear today; needs to up his game.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Came good for current stable at third attempt, with fairly comfortable success at Ripon (6f, good) in June, and recovered from awkward start to take third off today's mark at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) last month; must be considered.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Denied clear run when fourth of six on last month's stable debut at Windsor and went close at Chepstow (also 6f, good to firm) two weeks ago, despite rider losing iron inside final furlong; gets another chance off same mark here; deserves a change of luck.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Registered Group 1 wins at Longchamp last October (2m4f Cadran, very soft) and this May (near 2m, soft) and every bit as good when short-headed at Ascot (good to firm) earlier in May; 7-1 for the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot (2m4f, good to firm) nine weeks ago and raced in second for a long way before cracking in the final 2f (vet reported signs of heat stress); concedes 3lb all round today but tried to go head-to-head with the best stayers around last time and they are now absent; good chance if back to form.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: No ground worries; pretty reliable and got back on the scoresheet at Meydan (1m6f Group 3) in February, with a creditable second here in the Yorkshire Cup in May; 22l seventh in Gold Cup at Royal Ascot (2m4f; 125-1) nine weeks ago when, unlike Caballo De Mar, he never figured; second (short-headed) and third in the last two editions of this race and has a place chance again.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Tremendous progress last season; odds-on flop when rather forced to make the running in the Yorkshire Cup here on 2026 return; ran on nicely for a creditable sixth of 12 in a very strong Hardwicke at Royal Ascot (1m4f) next time but unseated leaving the stalls with a mishap in the Goodwood Cup (2m; 17-2); that leaves his stamina unproven but he stays at least 1m6f; unraced on softer than good to yielding; a leading contender if he gets this new trip and there's fair chance he will.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Probably acts on soft; 1m7f Group 3 winner in France in 2024 and third in a 1m4f German Group 1 last year; sold for 400,000euros last November and got off the mark over hurdles (second attempt) in a maiden at Galway three weeks ago, but his only run on the Flat for this yard was a poor one in the 2m5f Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot (11-1); others look more solid.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Unraced on softer than good except when well beaten on debut; smart performer on his day, beaten a neck by Illinois in the 2m5f Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot two starts back; far from disgraced when 33-1 fourth in the 2m Goodwood Cup last time and the return of blinkers (replacing recent cheekpieces) might add a bit of zip, but he's probably a place proposition at best.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: The supremely reliable performer (acted on any going) of 2024 and most of 2025 has gone and most of his performances since have been pretty grim in comparison; this season's clear exception was when he made class tell with his sights lowered in the 2m5f Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot, winning by a neck from French Master; the Goodwood Cup took him well out of his comfort zone again last time and he carried his head awkwardly, but the less demanding company today offers a bit of hope.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Close Listed third here (1m6f, good) on penultimate start and got up close home in a slowly run Group 3 over that same C&D (good to firm) on latest; he's never ventured beyond that and it's questionable whether it will suit; also needs a bit more improvement but he's regularly proved capable of that.

RaceName: Weatherbys Lonsdale Cup Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Has won on almost any going; front-runner at his best and he's a fine sight when in full flow, including with a win in this race in 2022; well beaten in it, however, in 2023 and 2024; in fact something was missing in all his first three races in 2024 and although he ended that campaign winning a minor race that September, he's not been seen since; it would be some feat if he could return with a win.

RaceName: British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Sea The Stars colt; fourth foal; dam French 11.5f winner, half-sister to winners Hunter's Light (1m1f/1m2f Group 1) and Linda Radlett (useful 9.5f-1m4f; dam of 1m4f Group 2 winner Fanny Logan), out of 1m2f winning half-sister to 12.5f Group 2 winner Courteous; looks the part on paper and he's a striking newcomer for yard with 42% record with 2yos this season.

RaceName: British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: 100,000euros yearling; sixth foal; half-brother to winners Venencia (8.5f/9.5f including French AW 2yo/US turf stakes; RPR 108), Pop Life (French 1m2f/1m5f) and Twolatebabydoll (US 5.5f turf); dam French 11.7f winner, out of French 7f Listed winner; yard 15% with 2yos this season and he needs watching in market on debut.

RaceName: British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: 160,000gns breeze-up 2yo; ran green at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm; 16-1) last month, but he kept on well and was beaten less than 2l in fifth of six; that form isn't strong but he should know more this time and is a likely improver; respected.

RaceName: British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: 80-1 on Yarmouth debut (7f, good to firm) last month and he faded into a well-held last of six; finished behind Majestic Jude in that race and he's probably one for later on.

RaceName: British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: 50-1 and he finished tailed off in last of eight on recent C&D debut (good to firm).

RaceName: British EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Didn't live up to market expectations on Sandown debut (5-1) last month and he was well held again when fourth of six at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) last week; still early days but others are more persuasive.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Now back on same mark as for narrow C&D (good) win just over a year ago but this season's record is unconvincing (last month's C&D third of four came in a tactical contest) and he refused to race here 17 days ago.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Placed twice off higher marks on AW this year but has become inconsistent and was soundly beaten on latest outing five weeks ago; also disappointed on only previous turf start (in May 2025); not an easy one to predict in first-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Won this race on good ground a year ago and followed up on soft ground over C&D a week later; not in same form this season but handicapped accordingly now and was placed over C&D (good) on last two outings; ought to make her presence felt again.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: In good form over C&D this summer, most recently when keeping on well for narrow win on good ground 17 days ago; probably doesn't have much margin for error after 3lb rise but rain will aid her cause.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Very useful over middle distances in his prime; had been in the doldrums for a good while but, having plummeted down the weights, breezed clear to win comfortably by 12l here (1m, good) nine days ago; 9lb well in under 5lb penalty today; ought to be hard to beat.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Regressive in Ireland over last two seasons and made nothing better than a mildly encouraging stable debut when midfield at Chepstow (7f, good to firm) last month; needs a boost from the refitted cheekpieces.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to win this season but went close at Chepstow (7f, good) in June and was denied a clear run before keeping on over that C&D last month; enters calculations.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: All six starts on good/good to firm; he's found one too good in 6f Group 2 races on his last three starts and there's the worry the same thing will happen today; however, it's possible the winners he has bumped into are better than the rivals he faces here, and perhaps the first-time cheekpieces will eke out something extra; he can be bang there once more.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Suited by the step up to 6f with 2l Listed third to Arapaho Gold at Newbury (good to firm) last month and improved again when runner-up in Group 3 at Deauville (6f, good) since; bumped into an exciting filly in France and could have a part to play; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Won in good style at Thirsk on first two starts (5f/6f, good to firm) and took the rise in grade in his stride when making it 3-3 in Listed race at Newbury (6f, good to firm) last month; deserves extra credit for that neck win from a Godolphin colt as he was hampered early; there can be optimism that this highly likeable prospect will continue to progress; key player.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: All four starts over 6f on good/good to firm; beaten only 2l when fading into seventh of 21 in the Group 2 Coventry at Royal Ascot and readily got off the mark when 1-6 for a maiden at Thirsk (6f, good) last Friday; this flat track could suit better than Ascot and he's not ruled out each-way.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Runner-up on debut (5f, AW) before going one better at Hamilton (5f, good), and he belied his 66-1 odds when keeping on for a fine third in the Group 3 Molecomb at Glorious Goodwood (5f, good to firm) last month; the step up to 6f could be a positive and he might not be far away.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: 525,000gns yearling who is a brother to 7f Listed winner Saber Strike; Aidan O'Brien second string when eye-catching second of 19 at 14-1 on recent debut at the Curragh (6f, good to firm); takes a swift leap in grade here but he's the sole Ballydoyle runner and could be a very bright prospect.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Impressive on debut at Beverley (5f, good) in April and followed up by a short head from Ronson in a conditions race there (5f, good to firm) in May; a sizeable step forward is needed on this first run since but the Gimcrack has been the target and his trainer has won this four times; could go well.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Promising third on debut over C&D (good) in May and built on that when third of 21 in the Group 2 Norfolk Stakes at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) two months ago; his strong finish last time firmly suggests today's return to 6f will be ideal and he's on the shortlist.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Went close on debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) in June and made all at Ascot (6f, good to firm) last month; today is a much tougher test of his credentials but his dam was a 5f Listed winner and his respected trainer has stated he has "masses of scope to go on in the future"; not ruled out.

RaceName: Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: All four starts over 5f on good/good to firm; 5l win at Beverley on second run before near-miss behind Matteo there and 2l fourth in Listed race at Sandown last time; it seems likely his limitations will again be exposed.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Constant progress last year saw her win four nurseries (5f, turf/AW) and she completed her season with a creditable fourth of 19 in a Listed event at the other Newmarket track (6f, good) in October; may have needed her reappearance run over C&D (good to firm) last month but that was a heavy defeat and she needs to find more progress to defy this mark.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Versatile ground-wise and she recorded her ninth win when bouncing with a comfortable success over C&D (good to firm) in June; still looks feasibly treated on that form and she was a fair third in a Class 3 event back here last month; respected dropped back in grade.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Two wins from three starts on AW and latest was off 6lb lower at Southwell (6f, AW) in April; 0-6 on turf but she made a bold bid at Chester (third of 11) last month and backed that up with a clear second at Ffos Las (5f, good) last time; this step back up in trip is a positive and she still has scope for further progress; key player.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Struggled in Class 3 event at Glorious Goodwood three weeks ago, but she's a C&D winner who was runner-up here (6f, good to firm; first-time visor) on her penultimate run; has claims if she can recapture that form and her last three wins have been under George Wood.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Often leads and her last three wins have been over C&D, including in this race last year; finished down the field in last four runs but this is a drop back in grade and she's now 7lb lower than for her last success; one to keep an eye on.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Made it second-time lucky when winning a Lingfield novice (7f, AW) in May, but she's been disappointing in three runs since; took a strong hold in a York handicap (7f, good to firm) last time but she needs a major revival on this switch to sprinting.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Has a patchy profile but she won at Lingfield (5f, good) in May and got back on the scoresheet with a narrow success at Yarmouth (5f, good to firm) last month; well-held second over this trip at Lingfield last time, but she got hampered at the start and that was behind a big improver; shortlisted.

RaceName: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won a Kempton maiden (7f, AW) in January but she's been expensive to follow otherwise, getting turned over at 3-1 or shorter five times; finished a close fourth with cheekpieces added at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) last week but that was a Class 5 and this is a deeper race; needs to find more.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up all four starts this season, most recently when losing out only by a neck on handicap debut at Southwell (7f, AW) last month; should be fine back on turf and has another big role to play on these terms.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up in two nurseries (both 1m, AW) for George Boughey in the autumn but failed to build upon satisfactory reappearance run (7f) when well-held fifth of six in Southwell handicap (1m, AW) in April; makes stable debut (same owners) after 138-day break and with a point to prove.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up on debut at Goodwood (6f, good) in October and probably didn't have race run to suit when third of four on reappearance outing at Pontefract (6f, good) in April; absent for another four months since and would be getting weight from her rivals if this was a handicap but is open to improvement over the new trip.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Rose far above his previous form when second of 17 to Asfoora in this race (100-1) last year in first-time cheekpieces but their effect was fleeting and subsequent runs, including in a handicap, don't offer much hope today; has now been gelded.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Said goodbye to handicaps when winning over C&D in May 2025 and just two runs later he won the Group 1 King Charles III at Royal Ascot (good to firm; handles good to soft); off the track for nearly a year after and he's been slowly working his way back to form since, looking more his old self when winning a Group 2 at Glorious Goodwood latest; a likely force.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Has won on soft and yielding ground but best on good or quicker; came from the clouds before meeting trouble in running in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot, so did well to finish about 3l behind the winner; again came from behind when leading near the line in a Group 2 at the Curragh since; in prime form but those tactics can be hard to pull off here.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: MPS Racing Ltd & The Ayrshire Tradesmen
Spotlight: Handles most ground; best form when winning a Group 2 on good to soft at Glorious Goodwood in 2025 and although he hasn't nailed it in the same way this year, the recent rain could give him a toehold into this race; visored once as a 2yo, now goes in blinkers.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Has taken time to get to grips with turf and was easily seen off when fourth in this last year; however, a gelding operation in the close season has worked wonders and he followed a Group 3 win with one in a Group 2 at Haydock (5f, good to soft), overcoming a slow start to win in some style; his star has dimmed somewhat at Royal Ascot and Goodwood since, but the return to a flat track offers hope that he can be on song again.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Some good efforts over 5f this year but he has met his match in Group races won by Rumstar, Cover Up and American Affair on his last three starts and has it to prove in this company.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: All turf races on good or quicker ground; best form when narrow winner of a C&D Listed race in July but his sights are raised much higher today in this, his first Group race.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Has four Group 3 wins (on good and good to firm) under his belt; outward appearances suggest this level is beyond him but if the door had opened in time for him in this last year he might have been placed instead of finishing only fifth; frame chance.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Finished a close third in the 2024 running and went on to win the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint (5f, firm; has won on good to soft) later in the year; seen only twice in 2025 and it's been a slow process recapturing form but a recent close fourth to Redorange in a C&D Listed race (first-time visor, now discarded) in July was better; no surprise to see him go well at a price.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Front-runs; all turf races on firm and good to firm; an unknown quantity for the 5f 3yo handicap at Royal Ascot but not any more as he justified strong market support when keeping daylight between himself and his rivals throughout; this track should suit him even better and, if coping with the change in the weather, he would have a lot going for him.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Started the year with two Listed wins at 5f before charging up the stands' side to snatch the Group 1 King Charles III at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) from under Rayevka's nose; not the same horse in the Group 1 July Cup at Newmarket after (6f; had good form at the trip as a 2yo) where he wouldn't have won at 5f and was eased down; has a question mark now but he's capable of putting his stamp on this race if on song.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Made an indelible impression when taking Royal Ascot by storm in the King Charles III two years ago and adding two more Group 1s in 2025 with this race (good to firm) and the Abbaye (very soft); has held on to much of her ability in 2026, not far away back at Royal Ascot and going down narrowly to American Affair in a Group 2 at Goodwood recently, but it's not certain that she still has what it takes to add to last year's win.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Has not yet won above Listed level; anything but disgraced when mid-division in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot or when a close fifth to Redorange in a C&D Listed race after, but it's hard to see her in this picture.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Her tremendous progress was highlighted by a close sixth in the King Charles III at Royal Ascot (good to firm, probably acts on soft) but her hopes were ended by some interference in C&D Listed race won by Redorange next time; her finding a bit more even now can't be ruled out but this bar is high.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: His Highness The Aga Khans Studs S C
Spotlight: Stays 6f well but this looks her trip and, following a Group 3 win at Longchamp (soft) she so nearly held on in the King Charles III (good to firm) at Royal Ascot, where Mission Central was better positioned on the stands' side; has come from off the pace on her last two starts, which is a worry on this track, but she has a strong form chance.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: D Bevan And Mrs D Bevan
Spotlight: Won Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot in 2025, then finished a close third to Jm Jungle in a Group 2 at Goodwood (5f, good to soft); she's had a chequered 2026 but the return to Goodwood last time may have helped when again close up in third; needs to find more in this company.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Group 3 winner over 6f at Ascot as a 2yo and she ran her best race of the year back there when fifth of 22 in the Commonwealth Cup in June; has had excuses since and although she should have plenty to find at this level in only her second 5f run, at least the track will suit her front-running style.

RaceName: Coolmore City Of Troy Nunthorpe Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Out of a Listed winner on soft; has improved with each of three turf runs at 5f (good and good to firm) and picked up impressively in 2yo Group 3 at the big Goodwood meeting, considering she had to wait for a run; looks capable of better and has to be respected in receipt of a big weight allowance.

RaceName: Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Won a Goodwood novice (1m2f, good) for James Horton last May but she's generally struggled in handicaps since including in in Ireland this season; record is now 1-13 and she has something to prove for another new yard; cheekpieces worn last time are removed.

RaceName: Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Well-bred filly who was a good second on handicap debut at Redcar (1m2f, good) in May; flopped when 3-1 favourite at Newbury (took keen hold) last month but she lost a shoe and it is still early days; big player if she can bounce back.

RaceName: Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Added to her Newcastle novice last autumn when landing a Nottingham handicap (1m2f, good to firm) last month; held in third of four at Lingfield last time but that was a respectable effort in a tactical race and she should be in the mix again.

RaceName: Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Camelot filly who cost 65,000euros as a yearling; no impact at biggish prices in three novice/maiden events this season but this is more realistic and she needs watching in market upped in trip on handicap debut; hood reapplied.

RaceName: Racing TV Handicap
Spotlight: Has a patchy profile but he's won two of his last four starts including a last-gasp success at Brighton (1m2f, good to firm) two weeks ago; only 2lb higher here and he's a big player again if he can back that up.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Displayed clear promise on all three 2yo starts in the autumn but has been safely held in three handicaps this year (6f/1m); tried cheekpieces last time; blinkers are given a whirl here.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Northern raider who is yet to win this season but has slipped to a good mark and was persistently denied a clear run when midfield at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm; first-time visor) last week; rain will aid her cause and she can be dangerous if her luck improves.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed after only four runs and recent heavy defeat on handicap debut is best overlooked (became unsteerable after reins broke in early stages); needs to improve on her earlier form, though.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Didn't fire on Polytrack ten days ago but pipped a dual subsequent winner when opening account at Leicester (7f, good to firm) last month and is not yet fully exposed over this sort of trip; contender if quickly back on song.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Well down the field in her first three handicaps but ran well from the front when fourth in first-time blinkers over C&D (good) this month and has possibilities if the headgear continues to aid.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Well beaten when last of six at Haydock (1m, good) this month and has now been unplaced all six starts; will appreciate this drop in grade but still can't be recommended.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Came good at ninth attempt, in what has turned out to be a good race for this grade at Windsor (1m, good to soft) in June; should be fine over this shorter trip and will be favoured by any rain; major player.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Placed in both handicaps, more recently when running-on third at Lingfield (6f, good) in May; looks well worth another crack at a longer trip and features prominently in calculations.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Made the frame in her last three sprints, most recently when third at Salisbury (5f, good to firm) last month; unraced over 7f since low-key 2yo debut but stays 6f well and can feature if her stamina holds out.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Seemingly back in good form when third to Gal at Leicester (7f, good to firm; first-time blinkers) last month but two lesser efforts have followed (1m/7f) and she now has questions to answer again; headgear removed.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Ten-race maiden; gave good account when fourth over nearly 6f at Carlisle (soft) in June but did not get competitive at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) 12 days ago; back over this trip for first time since 2yo debut.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap
Spotlight: Showed no promise in her three qualifying races (5.7f-1m) and could be considered only if lively in the betting before this handicap debut.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won in great style at Haydock (1m4f, good; unraced on softer) last July and put up a bold show over C&D this May; having been a non-runner at Royal Ascot where the good to firm ground was deemed unsuitable, he ran on it at Newmarket seven weeks ago and disappointed; can go well if back to peak form.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Probably acts on soft; off four months (given wind surgery) before shaping as if back in good form when mid-division at Glorious Goodwood (1m2f) last month, not getting best of runs and finishing with more to give, which might also be encouraging for this first crack at 1m4f; needs a career best in first-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Made a winning stable debut from off the pace at Meydan (1m4f, good; acts on soft) in January but has finished no better than mid-division in his four starts since; has edged back to that last winning mark, which he also had when a close third in this race last year.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: R A Pegum And Paul Anthony Henry
Spotlight: First two wins were on heavy/AW; there have been a couple of disappointments in his eight-race career but he followed two AW seconds by winning a six-runner race at Thirsk (1m4f, good) two weeks ago; up 5lb in this much more competitive race but he won in clearcut style in first-time blinkers.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; it looked as if 1m6f stretched him when seventh of 16 at Royal Ascot (every chance 2f out) and that he probably remained in form; however, he again came up short when favourite back over 1m4f at Ascot on latest start; something to prove after that.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Soundly beaten at Epsom on Oaks day on sole start on softer than good; upped to 1m4f (good to firm) for his two starts since when third of eight at Ascot (made most) and second of ten under 7lb claimer at York, both solid efforts but a bit extra will be needed to win this; non-runner at Newmarket yesterday.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Floundered on testing ground in the last two November Handicaps at Doncaster but he ran well on soft at this track in October 2024; well-backed favourite off a good mark when he reappeared over C&D (good) in May and he scored smoothly, in charge from 2f out; off since and back up 7lb but has to be considered seriously.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Placed twice on soft last year; beat only one home in a top 1m2f handicap here in July but in career-best form over 1m4f (good to firm) either side of that when winning at Newmarket and second in Shergar Cup race at Ascot; needs some respect.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Acts on good to soft but unraced on soft since 2024 (trained was positive about it last September); no shortage of success beforehand but cheekpieces seem to have worked very well on last two starts when winning at York (1m2f, good) and running on well again for second at Southwell (1m4f, AW); raised another 3lb but came from an unpromising position last time and still has more to give.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Had wind surgery in January; he's since had three runs this summer and something has clicked in a major way on last two occasions as he registered a ready win in four-runner race at Catterick and had no problem making all in a five-runner race at Newbury (again 1m4f on good to firm) six days ago; has a 5lb penalty and this is a vastly more competitive race, but never better.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Two hurdle wins last autumn seem a pretty meagre return for his respected yard but he was unlucky when a strong-finishing third in the 2024 Chester Cup (2m2f) and much the same can be argued for his fourth in this race last year when denied a clear run at crucial stage (3lb lower today); usually makes inroads far too late, as in the Chester Cup and Northumberland Plate last two outings, and stall 1 demands some luck here, but a sound pace up front could bring him into the equation.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: No ground worries but his career highlights (1m4f/1m6f) were in 2024, including a win in this race; 6lb lower today but that's after a rather muted 2025 when still with Roger Varian and his form went badly the wrong way in three runs this January-April for new connections; tongue-tie and/or cheekpieces, both fitted for the first time, need to work the oracle.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Formerly with Aidan O'Brien and Denis Hogan; well held on the Flat in Ireland this April; had wind surgery after failing to land the odds (bled from nose) in a maiden hurdle in June on debut for Faye Bramley; no mistake at 1-2 in a similar event at Stratford in July, which is far removed from today's task, though, and a big career best is needed on this.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) last month for Jack Morland and, following a 22,000gns sale, he was back with his former yard when following up in 15-runner race at Ascot (upped to 1m4f, good to firm; always close up) four weeks ago; back up another 7lb but his peak 2024 form (a win on good to soft here) was better still; on the shortlist.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Acts on soft; unproven beyond 1m and unraced beyond 1m1f until he tried 1m3f at Southwell (AW) 15 days ago and led 2f out until three rivals went past in the final 1f; that was a good run and his dam won at this trip but others clearly have less to prove in this hot 1m4f race.

RaceName: Assured Data Protection Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Made all, just holding on, in a novice at Windsor (1m2f, good to soft) in June on second start and the runner-up is 2-2 since; front-running fourth in a 1m3f novice at Kempton (AW) 16 days ago was creditable; dark horse but much more is needed in this hot race for handicap debut.

RaceName: End Of Summer Season Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 0-7 in Ireland but he's been a big improver this season and made it 2-3 for George Scott when completing a double at Hamilton (1m4f, good to firm) last month; that was against two rivals but he won in decisive fashion and still looks feasibly treated off 5lb higher; strong contender in hat-trick bid.

RaceName: End Of Summer Season Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: On same mark as when dead-heating at Southwell (1m4f, AW) last April but he's 0-15 since; finished runner-up in a big field at Newbury (1m4f, good) in May but he's hard to predict and was never involved at Ascot last time; comes with risks attached.

RaceName: End Of Summer Season Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 3yo who completed a double when landing a Class 4 handicap over C&D last month; well held in two quick-fire runs at Glorious Goodwood but he's back in calmer waters now and is a player if he can get back near best; acts on good to firm and good to soft.

RaceName: End Of Summer Season Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt when scoring under a prominent ride on handicap debut at Epsom (1m4f, good to firm) last month; up 6lb but that was a comfortable success and he's open to more progress over middle distances; respected.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-11 and has stamina to prove over this new trip but scores good marks for her consistency in handicaps at up to 1m this season; a possible.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Without a win since summer 2024 and nothing like the force of old but placed in this grade on last three appearances; drops back in trip after looking stretched by 1m4f last time; ought to be right in the thick of things.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-5 for new stable this year; ran quite well when fifth of ten in Leicester handicap (1m2f, good to firm) last month but was soundly beaten at Chepstow three weeks later; others have more pressing claims.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Mrs Muriel Forward & Dr G C Forward
Spotlight: Placed on three of her five starts since returning from long layoff this year, including C&D (good) handicap third two starts ago; likely to pose a potent threat in this basement grade.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Needs to rebound from a poor handicap run here nine days ago but is generally very consistent; came second in similar race to this over C&D (good) in June and probably won't be far away.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Temperamental maiden who was a well-beaten 150-1 shot in this grade here (1m) last month, having lost many lengths at the start when reluctant to race (not for the first time).

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Went close in Chepstow handicap (1m, good; fine over 1m2f) in June and has strong form claims here if judged on that performance but this regressive and inconsistent 6yo is on a long losing run, and his habit of starting slowly is always a worry; sports first-time cheekpieces; risky.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Yet to show any worthwhile form after six runs (two in bumpers), and was beaten about 28l when dropped to this grade at Chepstow (1m) last month; tries cheekpieces today.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Not disgraced over 1m2f in this grade on last two starts but is yet to be placed after 14 starts and needs to find something extra on this drop back in trip.

RaceName: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes
Spotlight: A maiden after 14 starts but looked suited by step up to 1m2f when coming from the rear to go close in this grade at Lingfield (good to firm) three weeks ago and has each-way claims at least if in similar form.

RaceName: Why Settle Technology AI Adoption EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton 2Yo Series Qual') (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Posted a useful effort when third in Superlative Stakes at Newmarket (7f) in July and not disgraced with fourth of six in Vintage Stakes at Goodwood (7f) since; this son of Frankel should prove at least as effective over 1m; he's very much the one to beat back in maiden company.

RaceName: Why Settle Technology AI Adoption EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton 2Yo Series Qual') (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Shaped encouragingly when a debut third in 6f Ayr maiden but failed to build on it when fourth of five in 6f maiden here last month; this Churchill colt goes up in trip and retains potential, but improvement is needed.

RaceName: Why Settle Technology AI Adoption EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton 2Yo Series Qual') (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to 1m2f winner Wildcitydiva (RPR 57); dam, maiden from 7f-1m2f (60), is closely related to 1m 2yo winner Dancing Granny; the market can guide for this daughter of Nathaniel on her first run.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 50,000euros breeze-up buy; fifth foal; half-brother to winners Campaign Trail (1m4f-2m Flat, RPR 91; 2m1f/3m2f hurdle) and Green Gate (German 1m4f); dam German 1m1f/1m3f winner, half-sister to 2m4f Group 1 winner Colour Vision; everything would suggest he'll improve for longer distances but the trainer factor heightens interest for sure.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: £62,000 yearling by Brocklesby winner Persian Force; 13-2 for AW debut at Kempton (7f) where he momentarily threatened before going down by 2l; has to improve plenty on that effort in this much deeper contest.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Positives to take from both his runs at about 7f (good to soft/good to firm) without suggesting he'll be capable of getting competitive in a maiden of this strength.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 150,000gns yearling; third foal; half-brother to winners Goldwork (6f 2yo; RPR 80) and Stitching Wheel (1m6f; 73); dam French 7f winner (82), half-sister to winners Broderie (German 1m Listed) and Great Esteem (useful 1m4f); stable's 2yos have been going well all season and it makes sense to check the betting with Speyside from the same yard.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Entered in the Group 2 Royal Lodge and Group 1 Dewhurst; travelled well but seemingly found out by inexperience when a beaten odds-on favourite at Sandown (7f, good to firm); that form has been franked and let down in the last week, but this Kingman colt is open to any amount of improvement with that run under his belt, especially when evidently held in high regard.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Did have a Gimcrack entry and still engaged in other Group races; has come up short in two races over 6f (good to firm/good; the latest a valuable maiden at Glorious Goodwood) but those front-foot finishes suggest this extra furlong could make a big difference to him; firmly in calculations.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: 550,000gns yearling by star stallion Night Of Thunder; sixth foal; half-brother to winners Dhabab (Group-placed 5.5f-7f; RPR 114) and Celeres (French 10.5f); dam unraced half-sister to 6.5f-1m Listed winner Boomshackerlacker; one of the more appealing newcomers on paper, and trainer has introduced some smart horses at this track down the years.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 24,000gns yearling, 110,000euros breeze-up purchase; fourth foal; half-brother to winners Zappata (7f/1m; RPR 74) and Crimson Rambler (1m/8.6f; 72); dam 1m/1m2f winner (99), half-sister to useful winners Shediak (6.5f-1m) and Shehira (1m); has been gelded; likely best watched.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 150,000euros foal, 400,000gns breeze-up buy in April; first foal out of an Italian 1m winner and sister to winners Call Me Love (Italian 1m2f Group 2) and Cloud Free (1m); tongue tied for debut; stable won this in 2021 with Hoo Ya Mal (had the benefit of a run) who went on to finish second in the Derby; perhaps a slight concern that stable jockey Oisin Murphy is riding for Hugo Palmer.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Wootton Bassett colt out of the stable's Group 1 winner Hydrangea; has multiple Group-race entries; beaten by a likely smart stablemate on debut (7f, good to firm) and, although turned over from the front when odds-on at Killarney (1m, good), he was only a length off City Of Dubai who has since gone close in a Listed race; has a very similar profile to the yard's last two winners of this (2023 and 2025) who stepped up plenty on their third starts; now goes in cheekpieces; strongly considered.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Price increased from 82,000euros as a foal to 170,000euros as a yearling; fourth foal; brother to 5f/6f winner Amiata (RPR 89) and half-brother to Norwegian 6f-10.7f winner Icon Bling (107); dam 6f winner (72), closely related to two 5f 2yo winners; makes debut in fairly deep waters and others appeal more.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 210,000gns yearling; 100-30 at Ffos Las (6f, good) and finished a shade over 8l behind the favourite who was ninth in the Coventry; this colt was slowly away and should be all the wiser here, but this demands significant improvement from him.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Blue Point colt who defied odds of 40-1 when 3l third in a strongly run 7f maiden at Glorious Goodwood (good to firm), faring best of the newcomers from a midfield position at halfway; entered in the Group 1 Dewhurst and the fact that Oisin Murphy rides when Andrew Balding is represented raises expectations.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Convivial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 60,000gns yearling; first foal out of a 5.4f 2yo winner (RPR 68) and half-sister to 6f winner Peony; this race is a tough starter but stable is having a good season with 2yos and this colt is in the Two-Year-Old Trophy.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Reliable mare who won won at Newcastle (7f, AW) in March and has finished a close fourth at Lingfield and over C&D (good to firm) in her last two starts; this is competitive against some progressive 3yos but she's been as good as ever this year and should go well again.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Improved her record to 2-5 when reappearing with a 33-1 win in Newbury handicap (7f, good to firm) in June; 5lb higher after another break, but she held off a subsequent winner last time and is open to more progress; respected.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Unexposed 3yo who added to her Southwell novice win when prevailing in a tight finish over C&D (good to firm) two weeks ago; up 3lb for that narrow success but that was a clear personal best and she showed a good attitude when it came to the crunch; shortlisted.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Made all for comfortable success in a Yarmouth maiden (7f, good to firm) last month but that was a five-runner race and she struggled in handicaps in her first two runs this season; still unexposed but she needs improvement to make a serious impact in this competitive event.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Made it second-time lucky with a narrow success in a Southwell novice (7f, AW; 6-1) last month; this is a different test on handicap/turf debut but she looks on a fair mark and is bred to be useful; one to keep an eye.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced 3yo who was awarded the race after being hampered in a Nottingham maiden (6f, good to firm) last month; needs to kick on again to defy this opening mark but she still has potential and this step back up in trip looks a good move.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Has been generally progressive in her eight starts and she got back on the scoresheet when landing a Yarmouth handicap (7f, good to firm) last month; another solid effort when second at Lingfield last time but this is a deeper race and she's more exposed than the other 3yos in this line-up; others preferred.

RaceName: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Now 2lb lower than for her Yarmouth win (6f, soft) last October but she's been out of sorts in last three runs and overall record is now 1-14; opposable.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Recorded a third AW win in July; didn't run badly at Galway over 1m4f (yielding to soft) and his lesser effort there next time is likely explained by the fact it came a day later; hood on for hurdling debut and not ruled out.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: A 1m2f AW winner for Jane Chapple Hyam last year; tailed off in two starts over hurdles so plenty of improvement needed.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Ex-Ballydoyle; won a Listed race at Lingfield last year; purchased for 78,000gns in October but has been soundly beaten in two starts over hurdles and two Flat races for new yard; needs to improve.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Three-time French bumper winner should win if she runs to her official rating of 117 but that was the thinking at Cork (2m3f, yielding) in April when sent off the 4-7 favourite and she finished tailed off; again tailed off in a Galway handicap hurdle last time; could bomb out or could win in a canter.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Finally won a point-to-point in April at the 12th time of asking; tailed off over 2m3f here on rules bow; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Touched off in a Down Royal Flat maiden last year (1m3f, good); made a mistake at two out when a 6.5l fourth at Ballinrobe last month (2m2f, good); runner-up over C&D last time when hampered by a faller at the last but it likely would merely have reduced the 14l winning margin; needs to progress.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Soundly beaten on debut in a bumper here and none too fluent on hurdles debut at Killarney last month; can only be watched.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Minor promise in bumpers but the same can't be said of his three maiden hurdle runs; best watched.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Stepped up from his poor point form when third on hurdling debut at Sligo (2m2f, good); ran poorly in a Navan bumper in September and was detached when falling at Roscommon earlier this month.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Tailed off in both maiden hurdle starts; third of five in a point-to-point in March; unlikely.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Best of four bumper runs came over 2m here in June when runner-up to a subsequent maiden hurdle winner; below best at Killarney last time; hurdles need to bring improvement.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Not much promise in two points but wasn't too bad on her rules bow at Galway when returning from over a year off to finish eighth of 19 (2m1f, good to yielding); place chance if building on it.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Nothing to recommend her based on four moderate runs at huge prices.

RaceName: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Relatively ignored in the market on her debut at Tramore and was tailed off; hood worn that day left off.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Veteran who won over hurdles in June and ought to have finished second here (2m, good; rider dropped hands in closing stages) when back on the Flat later that month; may need further than 1m4f nowadays, though, and younger rivals appeal more.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
OwnerName: Mike Harris Racing & Nikki Evans Racing
Spotlight: Two wins this year, the latter off 1lb lower at Bath (11.6f, good) in May; behind Buck Barrow when fourth over C&D (good) last month but that certainly wasn't a bad run; no surprise if he features.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Just held on to pip Adrian in C&D (good to soft) classified in June and has finished third off today's mark in two subsequent C&D handicaps (both on good); has obvious each-way claims again.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Regressive over hurdles; still lightly raced on the Flat and belied 40-1 odds when keeping on for third on handicap debut at Kempton (1m4f, AW) in May but has been well beaten twice since (11.6f/2m); now tried in a visor; not the percentage call.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Far too inconsistent to rely upon heavily but lost out only narrowly to Buck Barrow when clear second in C&D classified (good to soft) in June and is 1lb better off with that rival today.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Close third in tactical race when upped to this trip at Chepstow (good to firm) last month and has now made the frame in her last four handicaps; could still have untapped potential over 1m4f; shortlisted.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: A maiden after seven starts but would probably have preferred a stronger pace to aim at when keeping-on fourth at Southwell (1m3f, AW) last month; another 2lb lower here and has a fighting chance if first-time cheekpieces have positive effect.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Opened account at eighth attempt, with clearcut success in five-runner Brighton classified (1m4f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; that form isn't anything to get too excited about but the runner-up has won in that grade since and this filly might still have more to offer.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Struggled when a big-priced outsider for three novice races in the spring (1m2f-1m3f) but remains unexposed and has more realistic chance to get competitive in this low-grade handicap; cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap
Spotlight: Well beaten off basement marks in first three handicaps (all over 1m in blinkers); not bred to benefit from this hike up in trip and needs massive improvement; no headgear today.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Is enjoying an excellent season and notched a fourth success in 9f Musselburgh handicap in June; came in last of nine at Ayr (1m) last time but she's the sort to bounce back.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Gained a breakthrough success at Pontefract (1m) in July and backed it up with a good second of five in handicap at Ripon (1m2f) 18 days ago; a player off the same mark.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Julie & David Martin, Dan Hall & Partner
Spotlight: Made a winning start in handicaps over 1m here in May and doubled her tally at Beverley (8.5f) in July; posted a solid third of five at Nottingham (1m) last month; very much one to consider with this slightly longer trip a likely plus.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Fair maiden who has made the frame on all her five runs, fitted with cheekpieces when a good third of ten in 7f Wolverhampton maiden three weeks ago; not out of things now stepping up in trip on her handicap debut.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Mrs Tabor, Mrs Mv Magnier, Mrs Shanahan
Spotlight: Landed 8.5f maiden at Beverley on her return in April but she hasn't kicked on in handicaps, only ninth of 12 at York (7f) 27 days ago; she needs to take a big step forward.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive 1m winner at two; off nine months/had wind surgery before returning with a promising third of seven in 1m handicap at Redcar 23 days ago, staying on well late; big shout off the same mark.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: A fair 7f winner for Peter Chapple-Hyam in 2023; lightly raced since and well held at York (1m2f) and over hurdles at Uttoxeter last summer; not easy to make a case for on her comeback run here.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: A six-time winner (including here) in 2025; back in good nick of late, third of nine in 1m handicap here ten days ago; in the mix off the same mark.

RaceName: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Much improved of late and she readily completed a quick hat-trick in 1m2f handicap at Ripon six days ago; shoulders a 12lb penalty here but she's still not taken lightly in her current mood.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Improved on first two runs to be beaten 2l stepped up to 7f at Down Royal (good) 35 days ago; form has held up (fourth won maiden since) ; step up in trip could bring about improvement but needs to off this opening mark; stable first-string.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Standout effort on second start when beaten 1l in Leopardstown maiden (7f soft) in June, split two smart Ballydoyle fillies; step backwards over same C&D last time; steps up in trip and would look well treated on best run if bouncing back.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Finished ahead of Belicoso when second at Down Royal last month; placed twice again since and has built up some good experience; form of latest Galway effort looks solid; step up in trip should suit; Browne McMonagle prefers Belicoso but not much in it.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Well-held and slowly into stride on each of his three starts; step up in trip and gelding operation needs to sharpen him up; opening mark doesn't look too generous.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Landed a Cork auction maiden on debut over 6f on soft; beat Hanney Boy by 2l and he's been placed in Listed company since; last of 6 in Group 2 since on quicker ground; dam a winner over 12f so step up in trip could unlock further improvement and she looks on a exploitable mark.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Beaten between 8 and 12l in three decent maidens on good ground; shaped as if in need of further and bred to get it so makes some each-way appeal now in handicaps; tongue-tie on.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Couldn't get involved in three maiden runs from 6f to 7f; opening mark doesn't look too lenient so needs step up in trip to make a significant difference; first-time tongue-tie.

RaceName: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Huge prices on three maiden starts and ran accordingly; didn't fare much better albeit stayed on reasonably well on nursery debut when beaten 7.25l into seventh at Sligo 16 days ago; back up in trip now and mark probably too high.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Listed runner-up at Gowran Park (1m4f, good) last July and she's well handicapped on that form; following 360,000gns sale she may have needed the run on stable debut in Group 2 at Newmarket last month (first-time cheekpieces); however, she was tailed off and has something to prove after that; a tongue-tie is added.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who has an up-and-down profile but won a handicap at Newbury (1m2f, good to soft) last September and fared best of those to come from off the pace when third on her reappearance at Chester (10.3f, good) in May; returns from another break and slow ground would boost her claims.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 3yo who has been highly progressive and has continued the good work on her last two starts, with a 3l handicap second to Silver Lake at Goodwood (1m2f, good to firm) being followed by a Listed near-miss at Clairefontaine (1m4f, good to soft); there's every chance that she'll be bang there.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Easy win at Hamilton (1m1f, good) in May on second handicap run and soft ground may not have suited at Goodwood next time; creditable Listed third at Hamilton (1m3f, good to firm) since and that form has been boosted here this week; this progressive 3yo could have a big part to play if conditions suit.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who showed improved form in a first-time hood (retained) with close third of 14 at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good) last month; shaped on that occasion as though this first crack at 1m2f would be worth a go; might be involved; hinted at promise on soft ground on debut in 2024.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won Wolverhampton novice (9.4f, AW) last December and placed this year in her first four handicaps; close fourth at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) recently after two-month break but form has to go to a new level in this hotter contest.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Made all in a big field at Chester (1m4f, good) in May and is just 1lb higher today but she hasn't come up to scratch subsequently and others arrive with more pressing claims.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Improved upon her first three runs when upped in trip to win on handicap debut at Salisbury (1m2f, good to firm) last month and she followed up in dominant fashion at Glorious Goodwood (1m2f, good to firm); this unexposed 3yo could take a 9lb rise in her stride if conditions aren't an issue.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won at Southwell (1m, AW) in May on third start and, after heavy defeat on handicap debut at Royal Ascot, she beat her six rivals to win at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) last month; now back into a deeper race but this well-bred filly is in good hands to continue to progress; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Won three handicaps in a row in May/June at about 1m2f (good/soft) but has gone off the boil subsequently; needs to get back on track.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: HM The King & HM The Queen
Spotlight: Won Nottingham novice (1m2f, good to firm) in June on fourth start and she's since been a clear second to unexposed handicap newcomers in two small-field contests (1m2f, good to firm; subsequent winner Silver Lake on the first occasion); she may yet have a bigger performance in her.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: She's 5lb lower than when winning at Newcastle (1m, AW) in February and when running well at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) in June; she's 0-12 on turf and unproven at this trip, and she's been below par at favourite course Newcastle on her last two starts (1m).

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Front-runner who was runner-up over C&D (good) in May and third at Epsom (1m2f, soft) next time; made all in small field at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm) last month and, while she's up 3lb in a much hotter race today, she could continue to progress for her good yard; may make another bold bid.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won the Queen Mother's Cup for female amateur jockeys here (1m4f, good) in June; not beaten far when fourth of five at Hamilton (1m5f, good) since but there's a suspicion that this will prove too competitive.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Prominent racer who finished held in fifth of nine over C&D (good to firm) six weeks ago when last seen; however, she's won twice this season (1m/8.3f, good) and split two progressive fellow 3yos when second at Chester (10.3f, good) two starts ago; not discounted at likely big odds.

RaceName: Sky Bet EBF Fillies' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Second in this in 2024 (good to firm) and won at Southwell (1m3f, AW) in March but unplaced on her four starts since, well beaten at Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) most recently when reverting to turf following a break.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Returned from seven months off with a good second at Brighton and went one better at Sandown four weeks ago (both 1m on good to firm); 4lb rise manageable and Simon Walker a positive booking.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins over further for her former stable; operating off a reduced mark now but she was put in her place by Thiscouldbefun over C&D last week and could prove vulnerable again; blinkers back on after one run in cheekpieces.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Won the corresponding race 12 months ago off a 1lb higher mark (for today's rider); solid efforts on last three starts and he's a leading contender.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: The addition of blinkers saw him spring a minor surprise at Bath (1m, firm) in April; not at that level on his last three starts, most recently when ninth behind Marsh Benham at Sandown last month.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: He hasn't found his best form in three runs for Rod Millman but he is dropping down the weights and he has one of the more experienced riders on board; could revive.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Won two of his four starts (1m2f-1m4f) since joining Tony Carroll, including for today's rider; dropping back to 1m not sure to play to his strengths though.

RaceName: Taste The World Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
OwnerName: Mrs Wendy Jarrett & J S Moore
Spotlight: Made all to win a C&D handicap eight days ago; unpenalised for that win and officially 5lb ahead of the handicapper but it may not be quite so straightforward this time.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Placed three times in maiden hurdles at this venue before making all for an emphatic in a 2m contest here 13 days ago; no issue with this trip; others are much better suited by the race conditions.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Useful on the Flat in Britain, rated 89; made a winning start for this yard over hurdles at Killarney in May (2m1f, gd-yld); heavy defeat in a Punchestown novice too bad to be true; returned with a small graze on right-fore cannon bone, possibly picked up when blundering five out.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Not a big price in two point-to-points start but failed to complete; remote fourth over 2m4f on hurdling debut at Limerick; stepped up from that, winning a maiden over a shorter trip at Ballinrobe a month ago; second, third and fourth were from top stables; more on his plate now,

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Fair bumper form for Lorna Fowler without winning; produced an improved display to win a 2m Punchestown maiden in June; ran as well as could have been expected when taking third behind the two market leaders in a 2m4f Galway novice event.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: AQPS winner; joined Willie Mullins; left the champion trainer after five races to join Gordon Elliott; took advantage of a 10lb concession when much too strong for his former stablemate Beauvallon (odds-on) at Bellewstown; clear of the remainder when second to the smart Mullins-trained Witches Familiar at Galway.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Sent off favourite when winning a Tipperary bumper on good-to-yielding on debut last October; returned from seven-month break when third on hurdles debut over 2m3f at Cork in May; left clear at the last to land the odds in a 2m4f maiden at Limerick later that month.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Best form has been at Tipperary, where she won a bumper and was placed on her handicap debut last October; two unplaced handicap runs this season; faces an unenviable task at these weights.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Well-related mare; raced keenly and looked raw when fourth on debut in a bumper at Downpatrick in June; hooded now; tough task against experienced rivals.

RaceName: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle
Spotlight: Consistent at a modest level in handicap hurdles until below her best at Cork last time; this is very demanding

RaceName: Darley EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Fairly useful hurdles winner (at up to 2m6f) this summer who ran well very back on the Flat with fourth of 18 in 1m4f maiden at Galway 23 days ago; this Irish challenger is a player.

RaceName: Darley EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 5-1, hinted at promise when a never-dangerous fourth of eight in maiden at Ffos Las (1m, good) 17 days ago; this son of Sea The Stars fetched 485,000gns as a yearling and seems sure to do better, especially over this longer trip.

RaceName: Darley EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: RC Syndicate X and Gary Gillies
Spotlight: Palace Pier colt; fair form when runner-up on all his three starts this season, leading long way in nine-runner maiden at Windsor (1m2f) on latest occasion; holds very good form claims.

RaceName: CSG Rated Race
Spotlight: Debut juvenile winner at Leopardstown; started the season with two Group 3 runs at Curragh, not at all disgraced; however, she has been well beaten in two handicaps; others preferred as a consequence.

RaceName: CSG Rated Race
OwnerName: David K Kelly & Mrs Pauline Condon
Spotlight: Won over 1m on AW in France in February; unplaced in two subsequent races; best watched on Irish debut.

RaceName: CSG Rated Race
